claim.why_it_matters: 1.5 is a sibling of 1.1-1.4 (rendered ###) and 1.6 (###); at ## it outranks its parent `## 1.` siblings and breaks the outline.
claim.detail: Heading at the wrong level: should be `### 1.5 SEGMENTATION CLASSIFICATION` like `### 1.4 ORGANIZATION` and `### 1.6 SEGMENTATION CONTROL`.

verdict.reasoning: The printed page XVI-2 shows '1.5 SEGMENTATION CLASSIFICATION' in the same plain style as the other numbered subsection headings. Its number makes it a child of '1. INTRODUCTION TO THE SEGMENTATION MODULE' (## in the markdown) and a sibling of 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.4 and 1.6. The markdown renders those siblings as ### (lines 26091-26159 of specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md). It renders 1.5 alone as ##, which puts it at the same level as its parent. The heading text matches the PDF, so only the level is wrong. The defect is structural and does not change the normative text.
